correctness.rationale: The exact q-domain and edge language are stated. Four-character expansion plus Weil degree-3/4 bounds proves positivity for every q>=191. An actual compiled C++17 program exhausts all q<191, reduces all four-subsets by translation, verifies all sixteen sign patterns with bitsets, independently tabulates S4 minima, and verifies q27 via irreducible cubic representation. Five-round Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé equivalence to the random tournament holds iff all rank-five P4 extension axioms hold; q=3 is explicitly excluded because its P4 is vacuous.

value.rationale: This resolves the P4/S4 implication in a natural Paley subfamily, supplies an explicit complete membership test for the quantifier-rank-five random tournament theory, identifies the sharp eventual cutoff 107 and the nonmonotone failure at 103, and refines a much weaker prior large-field sufficient bound. The exact cutoff has clear structural and logical use, beyond mere numeric computation.
